steps.title: A reason to move
steps.body: Without downs, an offense could hold the ball forever. Downs force a team to ==keep gaining ground== or hand the ball over.

steps.title: Four tries, ten yards
steps.body: The offense gets ==four downs== to gain ==10 yards==. Reach the yellow line to gain and it earns a fresh set of four.

steps.title: 2nd & 6
steps.body: A 4-yard run on 1st & 10 makes it ==2nd & 6==: second down, six yards still to go. You'll hear the down and distance before every snap.

steps.title: Moving the chains
steps.body: Cross the line to gain and it's a ==first down==. The sideline crew moves the 10-yard chain to the new spot and the count starts over.
steps.note: Ref signal: an arm pointed toward the defense's goal line.

steps.title: Fourth down
steps.body: On 4th down most teams ==punt== it away or try a ==field goal==. Going for it is a gamble: come up short and the other team gets the ball right there.

steps.title: Turnover on downs
steps.body: Fail on 4th down and the defense takes over ==at that spot==. That's why short 4th-down plays are some of the most tense in the game.

steps.explain: It was 3rd & 6 and the run gained 4. Two yards short of the line to gain, so it's 4th & 2.

steps.prompt: It's 4th & 9 at midfield. What do most teams do?
steps.explain: Nine yards is a lot to gain on one play, and midfield is too far for most field goals. Teams punt to push the other offense back.
